mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with economic strengthening.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with tightening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase does not correlate with tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening consumer-driven economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in RSAFS and decrease in UNRATE does not correlate with economic strengthening.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with supply-side strengthening.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease does not correlate with weakening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during periods of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% QoQ and CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in GDPC1 and low CPIAUCSL does not correlate with economic strengthening.
